correctness.rationale: The zonotope determinant area formula and the absolutely convergent |sin| Fourier series give an exact nonnegative sum of squares for every n. The fixed-angle conditional mean \(2/\pi\) makes overlapping pair terms uncorrelated, giving exact moments. Orthogonality plus the multivariate CLT gives independent complex-Gaussian Fourier modes, squared to independent rate-one exponentials; a uniform L1 tail bound gives the full weak limit. The sine Euler product gives the exact Laplace transform. Exponential convolution and a telescoping infinite product give the sharp upper-tail prefactor \(16/(3\pi)\). Finite checker reproduces area/Fourier relations, Laplace values, and variance normalization; no finite experiment is used to prove an infinite theorem.

value.rationale: The studied area deficit is the canonical Euclidean isoperimetric shortfall of an equilateral zonogon from the disk at fixed deterministic perimeter. Its order-n geometric fluctuation scale, positive Fourier certificate, explicit non-Gaussian limit and exact sharp tail determine a natural infinite-family invariant not entailed by known moment formulas alone. The full distribution resolves a motivated gap between deterministic zonotope isoperimetry and generic nondegenerate Gaussian random-zonotope limit theory.
